newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV ENDS FIRMER AT 2,670-2,700 PER DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV ENDS FIRMER AT 2,670-2,700 PER DOLLAR.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 2,670-2,700 per dollar, up from 2,800-2,850 at the opening due to prevailing dollar supply and amid expectations of further lev gains, dealers said.
"Some banks sold dollars for levs ahead of tomorrow's deadline for the payment of minimum required reserves while demand lagged behind," said a dealer.
Local banks are currently required to place 11 percent of funds attracted the month before as minimum reserves with the central bank. The January payment deadline expires on Tuesday.

Traders said the market was generally more optimistic about the lev now that the new interim government had started action to fight the severe economic crisis and was preparing for talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

An IMF technical mission is expected to arrive this week for preliminary work and a negotiation mission is due on February 24 to resume talks on introduction of a currency board system aimed at hauling the country back from the brink of default.

The interim cabinet raised fuel prices by up to 178 percent, in force from Tuesday, to help Bulgaria's largest oil refinery Neftochim cope with a severe cash shortage which has prevented it from buying crude.

On Friday the interim cabinet, which inherited crippling fuel and grain shortages, banned fuel exports until April 30 and troops enforced border controls in a bid to curb smuggling by companies and private motorists. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
